events.title: Morbid Anatomy’s Krampus Market
events.description:
Join us for a delightfully non-traditional holiday market inspired by Krampus, the cloven-hoofed sidekick of St Nicholas who, in some parts of Europe, is infamous for mayhem and mischief during the Christmas season! Over twenty of our favorite vendors will showcase an exciting and unusual array of antiques, taxidermy, artisanal fashion, handmade jewelry, original art, gothic home decor, new and vintage books, and more. Find something for that hard-to-shop-for person on your list, and—if you’re lucky!—come home with something for yourself. But if you’ve been naughty this year, you’d better beware of Krampus and his birch branches!
We are delighted to offer special early access free to Patreon members ($15+)— enjoy exclusive first access to the market. After 11am, doors open to all shoppers for just $5.
There will also be opportunities to stop by our prize wheel for a spin and visit our Library for a look at the collection and special activities!
We look forward to seeing you!

events.title: Faces In Color | An Oil Portrait Workshop
events.description:
Explore how a few carefully chosen colors can bring a face to life.
This approachable introduction to portrait painting begins with a front-facing reference and a limited palette. We’ll break the face into simple shapes, explore basic proportions and feature placement, and learn how light and shadow give a portrait its depth.
Artist Kristina Dubrovskaia will guide you step by step, helping you mix colors, build light and dark areas, and develop an expressive portrait study. You’ll receive individual feedback throughout, with space to experiment and make your own color choices.
You’ll leave with a small oil portrait study and a clearer understanding of how to begin painting a face.
All materials and references are provided. Beginners and painters with some experience are welcome.

events.title: Engraving Service for Japanese Chopsticks @IPPIN Project
events.description:
Don’t miss the opportunity to personalize the Wakasa chopsticks at IPPIN Project!
IPPIN Project, in partnership with a Japanese Wakasa chopstick maker in Fukui, offers the chopstick engraving service again this year for a limited time!
If you’re considering a special gift for the upcoming holiday season, check it out and apply in-store or by email ASAP!!

For this reason, Japanese chopsticks come in various colors, patterns, and designs to distinguish one’s own. Even today, personalized chopsticks are popular gifts in Japan.
Order Period: November 1 to November 15
Available for pickup from early December
Store Location: Maker’s Guild at Building 5

events.title: Barrel Age Your Own Sake — A Brooklyn Kura Workshop Class
events.description:
Skill Level : Beginner-friendly, no coopering or sake knowledge required.
What You’ll Be Making : A handmade oak barrel, suitable for aging your own sake or shochu. The barrel will hold approximately 2 liters of liquid.
What You’ll Be Doing: You’ll assemble, shape, char, and personalize your barrel before filling it with a sake or shochu hand-picked by Brooklyn Kura for aging.
What’s Included? All barrel-making materials and tools, guided sake and shochu tasting flight, take your barrel home the same day
What To Expect
Right next door in Industry City, a small team is brewing junmai sake with some of the cleanest tap water in the country. Spend an afternoon with them and you’ll leave with two things: a handmade oak barrel built stave by stave with your own hands, and a palate for sake you didn’t have when you walked in. Char the inside with a torch, seat the heads, brand it with your initials — then fill it with something Brooklyn Kura hand-picked just for aging.
What You’ll Create
A functional 2-liter oak barrel, coopered from scratch — same craft, same tools, same afternoon of assembling staves and hoops, cutting crozes on the router table, and charring the interior until it’s ready for spirits. This time, what goes in it isn’t whiskey. It’s rice, koji, yeast, and water, aged into something you helped choose.
The Tasting Flight
A sake expert from Brooklyn Kura walks you through a flight of three sakes and a shochu, all brewed or distilled right here in Industry City, all selected because they take well to a little time in wood. The lineup changes with the seasons, but here’s what’s been on the table:
**Grand Prairie — a Junmai Ginjo built around white peach, jasmine, and toasted rice.
**Occidental — a dry-hopped Junmai, bringing out lychee, grapefruit, and cherry that age into deeper dried-fruit notes. Tidal — a fuller-bodied
**Junmai, all steamed rice, apple, and cereal bran.
**Kura Shochu — distilled from the leftover sake lees, rich with fig and custard and a rice umami built for barrel aging.
What Sake and Shochu Actually Are
Brooklyn Kura brews junmai-style sake — no additives, just four ingredients doing all the work. Rice sets the structure; the strain and how far it’s polished shape the flavor before brewing even starts. Koji, the fungus that turns starch to sugar, decides how sweet and umami-forward or light and aromatic the sake ends up. Yeast supplies the fruit, flower, and herb notes, which is why a batch often blends more than one strain. And water — helped along by some of the purest tap water in the country — is what makes the whole thing clean and crisp instead of muddy.
Shochu takes a different road. Where sake is brewed like wine or beer, shochu is distilled like whiskey or vodka. Kura starts with kasu, the leftover lees from sake-making, re-ferments it with a shochu-specific koji, and distills it into something rich and complex — closer to a young rice whiskey than anything else, and exactly the kind of spirit that rewards time in a barrel.
Finishing the Night at Kura
Your barrel’s made, your glass is empty — Brooklyn Kura is a short walk across Industry City, and your Craftsman Ave ticket gets you a discount on sake or shochu to take home and age. They’ve got a full kitchen too: mac and cheese, little smoky sausages, house-made focaccia. Good reason to stay a while longer.

events.title: Sake Tasting Event: Sake and Cheese Pairing Class and Brewery Tour
events.description:
Step away from that bottle of vino and join us to sample the absolute best beverage to pair with cheese – We are talking about sake! If you haven’t yet tried pairing craft sake and premium cheese, you are in for a revelation. We’ll explore a wide range of flavors and textures… and together, we’ll discover the most exciting combinations of sake styles and cheeses from around the world. The experience is fun, interactive and absolutely delicious! Join us at Brooklyn Kura to learn about sake where sake is made!
What’s included:
A welcome sake to get you started!
A brief intro to sake and cheese basics.
Guided Tasting of 5 Japanese craft sakes from different regions paired to perfection with 5 outstanding cheese varieties.
Exploration of sake and cheese production styles and terrior.
Enjoy some nibbles and spreads on your cheese board that will take the pairing over the top.
Handouts so you can bring your newfound sake and cheese knowledge home
Finish with a Guided tour through our new Sake Brewery
